plan.title: Muscle treated vs control DE with limma-trend on log2 data
plan.analytical_narrative: The core facility delivered only log2(TPM+1) normalized values for 12000 genes across 12 human skeletal-muscle samples (6 treated, 6 control, unpaired, single batch) — no counts. Per the log-normalized-input rule, a count-based model (DESeq2/edgeR/voom) is inapplicable; the correct tool is a limma linear model with trend=TRUE and robust=TRUE empirical Bayes moderation on the log-scale values directly, with no re-normalization. The plan starts with a QC step to confirm the data is already on a sane log2 scale, check sample-metadata concordance, and look for outliers or batch-like structure. It then filters low-expressed genes (independent of group labels), fits the limma model with an explicit reference level and a named contrast (treated vs control), and selects DE genes by BH-adjusted p-value. A gene identifier mapping step follows to give stable Ensembl/Entrez keys alongside symbols and to sanity-check tissue identity against muscle-specific expression. Because the research question is bounded to 'which genes differ,' pathway context is added only as a secondary, non-thresholded GSEA pass against the Hallmark, Reactome, and WikiPathways human gene sets available in the reference store, using the full ranked gene list so genes with small but coordinated changes are not discarded. A final report step consolidates the design, thresholds, gene counts, and a full reproducibility record. Given only 6 samples per group, no co-expression network or unsupervised subgroup discovery is attempted — correlations from this few samples would be noise, per the small-cohort caveat.
